systemPrompt:
# Aspiran content writer

You write short, interactive study pieces for Aspiran, an Android app where civil services aspirants study together. You write every piece in English and Hindi. Other languages (Telugu first, then Marathi, Tamil, Bengali and Kannada) are added later by translating your checked English, so you never write them here. An editor checks your draft before anyone sees it, so a gap you leave honestly is better than a fact you guess.

## Facts come only from the source

- Use only facts, numbers, dates, names and article numbers that appear in the text inside `<source>`. Do not add anything from memory, even if you are sure of it.
- Copy numbers exactly as the source gives them. Keep the source's hedges ("often", "about", "usually").
- If the source does not support a field, write less rather than inventing. For optional fields, use null.
- Name only sources that the source text itself names. If it names none, write exactly "Editor's source notes" in English and "संपादक के स्रोत नोट्स" in Hindi, and the editor will fill it in.
- Never invent a previous-year question, a quotation, a statistic or a story about a member.

## Voice

- Warm, plain and exact, like a good senior explaining over chai. Short sentences. No jargon without a gloss.
- Teach the static concept under the news, and say why it matters for the exam.
- Present political questions from both sides. Never tell the reader what to think about a party, a government or a person.
- Respect every word limit. Limits are counted in words, and they are hard limits.

## Tone

Pick the tone from the subject, not from how exciting it is.
- LIGHT: everyday or quirky topics (food, festivals, odd facts). Only LIGHT pieces may joke or use an emoji.
- NEUTRAL: most policy, polity, geography and economy.
- SERIOUS: security, disasters, health crises.
- TRAGIC: loss of life. No jokes, no emoji, no sound, and the piece is not shareable.

## Never write

- Urgency or scarcity: countdowns, streaks, "hurry", "last chance", "only 3 left".
- Promises: "guaranteed", "100% selection", "topper's secret".
- Hype or scolding. A wrong answer gets an explanation, never a put-down.

## Hindi

- Write natural Hindi as aspirants read it, in Devanagari. Use the standard terms: अनुच्छेद (Article), संशोधन (Amendment), धन विधेयक (Money Bill), संयुक्त बैठक (joint sitting), राष्ट्रपति की अनुमति (assent), मौलिक अधिकार (Fundamental Rights), लोकसभा, राज्यसभा, मानसून.
- Keep acronyms that aspirants use as is (IMD, LPA, GDP, UNESCO).
- Say the same thing as the English, in the same order, with the same number of list items and the same answer positions. Numbers stay as digits.
- Hindi may run up to a third longer than the English.
- Two registers. Content (facts, statements, options, exam-style questions, passages) is in standard Hindi. Anything that talks to the reader (the "why" explanation, tips, nudges, instructions, prompts to reflect, guided steps) is in colloquial, spoken Hindi, the way a friendly senior would say it, with the everyday English words aspirants use (exam, mock, revision). It is still respectful (आप), free of gender, and carries every fact and number.

## Output

Return one JSON object that matches the schema you are given, and nothing else. Every `en` field has a matching `hi` field.

registry.note: One entry per content type. Each folder holds schema.json (the full pack), fill.schema.json (what a writer or model fills), config.json (knobs and defaults), brief.md (instructions) and example.json (a valid pack).

choose.title: Choose
choose.sfx: Tick on a pick, a santoor chime when right, a soft nudge (never a buzzer) when wrong.
choose.motion: The picked option settles in 150 ms; the explanation rises in 200 ms.

sort.title: Sort into buckets
sort.sfx: A whoosh as a card flies to its bucket, a snap when it lands, a nudge if it bounces back.
sort.motion: Cards fly to the bucket in 300 ms; a wrong one bounces back with a 400 ms wobble.

order.title: Put in order
order.sfx: Tap to pick, a wooden snap as each tile locks, a chime when the line is complete.
order.motion: Tiles spring into slots (300 ms, slight overshoot); values count up as each locks.

match.title: Match pairs
match.sfx: Tick on a match, a nudge on a miss.
match.motion: Matched pairs slide together and fade to the done colour in 250 ms.

reveal.title: Flip and reveal
reveal.sfx: A page turn on each flip; a chime on the last card.
reveal.motion: Cards flip in 400 ms (a swap with reduced motion); lines on the back appear one by one.

steps.title: Step through
steps.sfx: A page turn per beat; an optional soundscape under stories; a chime at the end.
steps.motion: Each beat slides in from the right in 300 ms; choices fold open in 200 ms.

compare.title: Side by side
compare.sfx: A tick as each row opens.
compare.motion: Rows slide in from both sides and meet in the middle in 250 ms.

hub.title: Link web
hub.sfx: A tick per spoke; a chime when all are open.
hub.motion: Spokes draw out from the centre in 300 ms when tapped.

cloze.title: Fill the gap
cloze.sfx: A snap when a word drops into a gap, a nudge if it doesn't fit.
cloze.motion: Words fly into gaps in 250 ms; a wrong one shakes and returns.

picture.title: Picture story
picture.sfx: A page turn per frame, a santoor chime on the frame that names the idea.
picture.motion: The camera pans across one illustration to each frame's focus point in 1.3 s; with motion off, each frame is a still crop.

examFormats.note: Every UPSC CSE Prelims and Mains question format, and the templates that practise it. Format descriptions follow the public exam pattern; they are not previous-year questions. Optional-subject papers are out of scope. The interview (personality test) has one format so far, covered by hidden-why.

papers.prelims-gs1: Prelims GS Paper I (100 MCQs, 2 marks each, one-third negative marking)
papers.prelims-csat: Prelims CSAT, GS Paper II (qualifying, 33%; 80 MCQs)
papers.mains-gs1: Mains GS1: Indian heritage and culture, history, geography of the world and society
papers.mains-gs2: Mains GS2: governance, Constitution, polity, social justice, international relations
papers.mains-gs3: Mains GS3: technology, economy, environment, biodiversity, security, disaster management
papers.mains-gs4: Mains GS4: ethics, integrity and aptitude
papers.mains-qualifying: Mains qualifying papers: Paper A (an Indian language) and Paper B (English)

formats.name: Direct MCQ
formats.desc: One question, four options, one right answer: a fact, a concept or an application.

formats.name: Negative stem
formats.desc: "Which one of the following is NOT ..." or "is incorrect". The trap is reading it as a positive question.

formats.name: Statements with codes
formats.desc: Two to four numbered statements, then "Which of the statements given above is/are correct?" with codes such as 1 only, 2 only, both, neither.

formats.name: Select the items (codes)
formats.desc: A numbered list of items, then "Select the correct answer using the code given below" (1 and 2 only, 1, 2 and 3 ...).

formats.name: How many statements are correct
formats.desc: Only one, only two, all three or none. Codes no longer help elimination, so every statement must be judged.

formats.name: How many pairs are correctly matched
formats.desc: Three or four pairs (place and state, term and meaning), and the member counts the correct ones.

formats.name: Statement I and Statement II
formats.desc: Two statements; decide whether each is true and whether II explains I. The older assertion-and-reason format.

formats.name: Statement I, II and III
formats.desc: Do Statements II and III both hold, and does each explain Statement I?

formats.name: Match List I with List II
formats.desc: Two lists matched with codes, or pairs matched directly.

formats.name: Arrange in order
formats.desc: Chronological order, north to south, largest to smallest, upstream to downstream.

formats.name: Location and map
formats.desc: Where a place, river, park or strait is, what it borders, which lies furthest east, and so on.

formats.name: Current affairs on a static base
formats.desc: A recent event used to test the concept behind it.

formats.name: Numbers, reports and indices
formats.desc: Who publishes which index, what it measures, and order-of-magnitude facts.

formats.name: Reading comprehension
formats.desc: A passage, then the main idea, an inference, the assumption behind it, or the most logical corollary.

formats.name: Basic numeracy
formats.desc: Percentages, ratios, averages, time and work, speed and distance, number properties.

formats.name: Logical and analytical reasoning
formats.desc: Syllogisms, direction sense, blood relations, arrangements, coding and series.

formats.name: Data interpretation
formats.desc: A table or chart, then questions that need a calculation from it.

formats.name: Directive-word answer (10 and 15 marks)
formats.desc: 150 or 250 words to discuss, critically examine, analyse, elucidate, comment and so on, with an introduction, a body and a conclusion.

formats.name: Reading the directive word
formats.desc: What "discuss", "critically examine" or "to what extent" asks for, and the mistake each invites.

formats.name: Diagram, flowchart or map in an answer
formats.desc: A quick sketch that carries the answer: a process flow, a cycle, a labelled map.

formats.name: Both sides and way forward
formats.desc: Arguments for and against, then a balanced conclusion and a way forward.

formats.name: Ethics concepts and thinkers
formats.desc: Define and distinguish terms (integrity, probity, empathy), and the contributions of thinkers.

formats.name: What does this quote mean to you?
formats.desc: A quotation by a thinker, to be explained in the present context with an example.

formats.name: Case study
formats.desc: A scenario with stakeholders, ethical issues, options with merits and demerits, and a course of action.

formats.name: Essay (philosophical or issue-based)
formats.desc: 1,000 to 1,200 words on a quote-like or issue theme, read across many dimensions, with a strong opening and close.

formats.name: Qualifying essay
formats.desc: A shorter essay in the chosen Indian language (Paper A) or English (Paper B).

formats.name: Précis
formats.desc: Reduce a passage to about one-third of its length, with a title, in your own words.

formats.name: Comprehension
formats.desc: A passage with questions answered in your own words.

formats.name: Translation
formats.desc: English to the Indian language and back, in Paper A.

formats.name: Grammar and usage
formats.desc: Correct the sentence, use a word or idiom, give a synonym or antonym.

formats.name: Talking about ideas in the interview
formats.desc: Explaining a concept or a piece of evidence clearly and honestly when the board asks for your view, including what the evidence does not show.

# Telugu (తెలుగు): style note

Status: pilot (the third language). Packs reach Telugu through translation files made from the checked English. A Telugu editor approves each file before it is shown.

## Register

- Modern standard Telugu (వ్యావహారిక భాష) as Telugu newspapers and Telugu Akademi textbooks use it. Not the old literary register (గ్రాంథిక భాష).
- Address the reader as మీరు, and keep it free of gender (no "విద్యార్థి మిత్రులారా" style address that assumes a group).
- Short sentences. Telugu runs to fewer, longer words than English, so word limits are rarely the problem; a line that is long on screen is. Keep it as tight as the English.

## Two registers

- Content (statements, options, exam-style questions, facts, passages, titles): modern standard Telugu, as above.
- Comments and instructions (the "why" explanation, tips, nudges, guided steps, questions to the reader): colloquial spoken Telugu, the way a friendly senior talks, with the everyday English words aspirants use (exam, mock, revision, syllabus, notes). Still respectful (మీరు) and free of gender.
- Example. Content: "ప్రాథమిక విధులు రాజ్యాంగంలోని అధికరణ 51A లో ఉన్నాయి." Comment: "ఇక్కడ చాలామంది తికమకపడతారు. 42వ సవరణతోనే ఈ విధులు వచ్చాయి, మొదట్లో లేవు. ఇది గుర్తుపెట్టుకోండి."

## Exam note, which matters for terms

- The Prelims papers are set in English and Hindi only. A Telugu-medium aspirant still meets the English term in the paper, so on Prelims-style pieces (statements, pairs, lists, options) give the English term in brackets the first time a technical term appears, for example ప్రాథమిక విధులు (Fundamental Duties).
- Mains answers and the interview can be in Telugu, so Mains-style pieces (answer skeletons, case studies, essays) use the Telugu term alone.

## Starter glossary (an editor confirms each term against the Telugu Akademi glossary)

| English | Telugu |
| --- | --- |
| Constitution | రాజ్యాంగం |
| Article | అధికరణ (ప్రకరణ in some textbooks; use one consistently) |
| Amendment | సవరణ |
| Parliament | పార్లమెంటు |
| Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha | లోక్‌సభ, రాజ్యసభ |
| Fundamental Rights | ప్రాథమిక హక్కులు |
| Fundamental Duties | ప్రాథమిక విధులు |
| Directive Principles | ఆదేశిక సూత్రాలు |
| Money Bill | ద్రవ్య బిల్లు |
| joint sitting | ఉమ్మడి సమావేశం |
| President's assent | రాష్ట్రపతి ఆమోదం |
| Supreme Court, High Court | సుప్రీంకోర్టు, హైకోర్టు |
| Election Commission | ఎన్నికల సంఘం |
| monsoon | రుతుపవనాలు |
| Emergency | అత్యవసర పరిస్థితి |

- Keep acronyms aspirants use as is (GDP, IMD, UNESCO, RBI).

# Calm now (breathing and grounding)

Schema: `upsc-pods/calm-script@1` · Folder: `content/calm-script/` · Family: Calm · Engine: steps

**Exam:** wellbeing · papers: none (study skill) · formats: none

**Sound:** No effects. The member may add a calm-tones or soundscape bed, off by default.

**Motion:** A circle grows on the inhale and shrinks on the exhale; with reduced motion it is a filling bar instead.

## How to fill it

A short guided exercise for a stressed moment: slow breathing, the double-inhale sigh, 5-4-3-2-1 grounding or a body scan. A human narrator records it later in English and Hindi. It sits beside "Need to talk?", never in place of it, and the app shows the support line from config on every script.
- No health claims. Say what the exercise is and let people judge how it feels. Never "cures", "heals", "treats", "therapy", "proven", "brainwaves", "anxiety disorder" or anything clinical.
- beats: short instructions, one action each. The seconds add up to about the minutes given (within a fifth).
- pace: for slow-breath, inhale + hold + exhale should come to 8 to 12 seconds (5 to 7 breaths a minute). For sigh, a short second inhale is the hold.
- Kind, plain words. No "relax!" commands, no "you should feel". Offer, don't instruct: "if it feels right, close your eyes".
- No sound effects. The optional bed (calm tones or a soundscape) is picked by the member, off by default.

# The Hidden Why

Schema: `upsc-pods/hidden-why@1` · Folder: `content/hidden-why/` · Family: Watch · Engine: picture

A Deepstash-style picture story with a Freakonomics question. 5 to 8 captions (16 words or fewer) over one 360x640 illustration, each with focus [x, y, zoom]; the first is a hook that sounds wrong, the last names the idea. Then named, sayItSmart (about 40 words, with the evidence), careful (what is contested), followUp {q, hint}, useItIn (1 to 3 papers) and sources (verify true until checked). Prefer Indian evidence. No invented quotes, no result claims.
